title: Add Unconsolidated guard to prevent instant deprecation of new records
description: P0 — MemoryStateMachine.Evaluate immediately deprecates new Unconsolidated records on first triage cycle. A fresh record (UsageCount=0, Confidence=0, References=[], LastUpdated=now) scores 0.1, which is below DeprecationThreshold (0.2). Every new memory created via the API is instantly deprecated and becomes invisible. Fix: add a guard in Evaluate that skips deprecation when original == MemoryStatus.Unconsolidated, or lower DeprecationThreshold below the minimum possible score for valid records. This is related to TSK-0344 (scorer weights fix) but is a separate guard that should be applied regardless of weight normalization. Found in 10-agent codebase audit 2026-07-10 (P0-001).

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Added guard in MemoryStateMachine.Evaluate: when original == MemoryStatus.Unconsolidated and score < DeprecationThreshold, stay Unconsolidated instead of being instantly deprecated. This matches the existing allowDeprecation pattern. Commit pending.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: 2026-08-08 deep-dive reverified that MemoryMaintenanceTasks.DeprecateObsoleteRecords directly deprecates every eligible low-scoring non-Deprecated record, bypassing the Unconsolidated protection in MemoryStateMachine. Add a fresh-record/startup-grace regression case before closing this task.
